props.gloss_en: the mishna: [when Shabbat falls on] all the remaining days, the lulav is six [days] -- i.e. it is not taken on that Shabbat
the mishna: when the first festival day falls on Shabbat, they bring their lulavim to the Temple Mount
the mishna: [the court] enacted that each and every one takes [his lulav] in his house
Rabbah: [the lulav does not override Shabbat as] a decree lest one take it in his hand and go to an expert to learn, and carry it four amot in the public domain
Rabbah: and that is the reason of the shofar [not sounded on Shabbat]
Rabbah: and that is the reason of the megilla [not read on Shabbat]
the first day -- the Rabbis enacted for it [taking] in his house [so the decree is not needed]
the [lulav of the] first day is Torah law [even] in the outlying areas
on the first day, which is Torah law in the outlying areas, the Rabbis did not decree
on these [other days], which are not Torah law in the outlying areas, the Rabbis decreed
we do not know the fixing of the month
those who know the fixing of the month [do] override [Shabbat with the first day's lulav] -- yes, indeed so
the other teaching: [on a first festival day on Shabbat all the people bring their lulavim] to the synagogue
learn from it: here [Temple Mount] -- when the Temple stands
there [synagogue] -- when the Temple does not stand
'and you shall take' -- that there be taking in the hand of each and every one
'for yourselves' -- from yours, to exclude the borrowed and the stolen
'on the day' -- even on Shabbat
'first' -- even in the outlying areas
'THE first' -- teaches that it overrides [Shabbat] only on the first festival day
Rava: ['on the day -- even on Shabbat'] is needed only for the lulav's facilitators, and according to this tanna
as taught: lulav and all its facilitators override Shabbat -- the words of R' Eliezer
and the Rabbis -- what do they do with 'on the day'? they need it for: by day and not by night
he derives it from the end of the verse: 'and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days' -- days and not nights
there, by sukka, [the mitzva is] days and even nights (the premise of the Rabbis' would-be gezera shava)
the baraita: 'in sukkot you shall dwell seven days' -- days, and even nights
